faq: What kind of old systems can you connect?
Desktop software with a database, on-premise servers, SOAP or XML services, and tools that only export CSV or FTP files. We check what access exists before you pay.
Will you change my old system?
No, not unless you ask. The bridge sits beside it and reads what it already provides. Any write-back is agreed in writing first and tested on a copy.
Do you need to log into my server?
We work through access you grant, such as a read-only database user or a shared folder. We never ask for passwords in chat, and you can remove our access any time.
What if the old system has no export at all?
Then we look at options such as reading the database directly or scheduled reports. If nothing safe works, we tell you before starting and no work is done.

desc:
Legacy system integration without a rebuild connects older software, databases and file exports to the modern tools you use today. Ecom Swift LLC builds a small, safe bridge that reads from the old system and passes clean data to your store, app or CRM.

## What is a legacy system link?

A legacy system link is a small program that sits between old software and new tools. The old system may only offer a database, a nightly file export or an outdated interface. The bridge reads from it, converts the data into a modern format and sends it where it is needed.

Nothing inside the old system has to be replaced. It keeps doing the job it already does well.

## Why replacing the old system is not always the answer

Old software often holds years of working business rules, and rewriting it is slow and risky. Staff know how it behaves, and the data inside is valuable. Yet it cannot talk to your online store, your CRM or your reporting tool, so people retype figures or export spreadsheets every week.

A bridge solves the communication problem without touching the core. You get the benefit of connected systems today and keep the freedom to replace the old system later, when you are ready.

## What changes when old and new are connected

The gain is mostly time and accuracy. Orders, stock levels or customer lists flow automatically instead of by hand, so there are fewer typing errors and fewer late updates. Online customers see figures that match the back office, because both read from the same source.

The bridge also gives you a future path. Once the data is available in a clean format, moving to a new system becomes a smaller project, because the export work is already done. The legacy system is protected in the meantime, since the bridge reads carefully and leaves it unchanged.

## What a good bridge includes

- A connection method that fits the old system, such as a database read, a scheduled file export or a legacy interface.
- Read-only access by default, so nothing in the old system is altered.
- Data cleaning that fixes odd date formats, character problems and duplicate rows.
- Conversion into a clean format that modern tools expect.
- A schedule you choose, with a clear report when a run fails.
- A backup copy of data before any write-back.
- A small API in front of the old system where two-way updates are needed.
- Written notes that explain how the bridge works and how to restart it.
- A list of data types moved, so scope stays clear.

## How we build it

We begin by learning what the old system can offer: a database, a file, a report or an old interface. We confirm which data types matter and where they should arrive. Then we build the reader, clean the data and send a small test batch to the new tool for your approval.

The Basic package gives you a read-only link that exports a couple of data types. Standard adds a scheduled bridge to one modern tool with an error report. Premium adds two-way updates where the old system allows them, a backup step and a handover call. If the system offers no export at all, we look for another safe route and tell you honestly what is possible.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Start with read-only access.
- Keep a backup of the data before any change.
- Choose the few data types that matter most.
- Write down how the bridge runs and who watches it.
- Test with a small batch first.

**Avoid:**
- Editing the old system directly to make the link easier.
- Moving every field just because it exists.
- Running the first sync on live data with no sample.
- Leaving the bridge without alerts.
- Depending on one person who knows how it works.

## Who it is for

A wholesaler with an older stock program wants products and quantities to appear in an online store. A clinic or workshop with a long-running database needs customer data in a modern CRM. A company planning a future migration wants the data flowing now and the old system retired later.

## What we need from you

Tell us what the old system is, what it can export and which data you want to move. Sample files or a copy of the database help us plan. We prefer a copy for testing and never need passwords sent in a message. Where server or database access is required, we agree a limited read-only user together.
